regions.text: 無限に繰返される同舗約圓形運動をなしてるる。

quote.translation: The poem okitsu tori (i) / kamo doku shima ni (i) / waga ineshi (i) / imo wa wasureji (i) / yo no kotogoto ni (i), by the contingent relation of a single rhyme held throughout, forms a recurring circular movement repeated without end.

regions.text: また加らごろもぎつつなれにしつましあれば欲るばるきぬる加びをしぞおもふといふ如き折句にあっては育語の意味上の理由性によつて貫かれた一首の全體に更に音韻上の偶然前闘係による他の新しい意味が二重に附加されてゐる。

quote.translation: In an acrostic such as karagoromo / kitsutsu narenishi / tsuma shi areba / harubaru kinuru / tabi o shi zo omou, again, a further new meaning is added, doubly, to the whole poem, which is already permeated by the groundedness of the meaning of its words, through a contingent relation of sound.

regions.text: 廻文はなかきよのとおのねぷりのみなめざめなみのりぶねのおとのよきかな」の如く上から護んでも下から確んでも同一の歌であるが、圓形運動によつて論理飽必然的開係以外に特殊な偶然性を生むところに暴に擧げた数142857などと頻似の性格を有つてゐろものである。

quote.translation: A palindrome such as nakakiyo no tōno neburi no mina mezame naminoribune no oto no yoki kana is the same poem whether read from the beginning or from the end, and in producing through circular movement a special contingency over and above the logical and necessary relation, it has a character similar to that of the number 142857 cited earlier.

regions.text: 寺田寅彦氏の「萬華鏡」に「英語や獨逸語と段々だ教はるうちに屢々日本語とよく似た音をもつた同義の語に出逢ふ事がある。

quote.translation: Mr Terada Torahiko, in his Mangekyō, writes: "As I was taught English and German, step by step, I often came across words of the same meaning with sounds very like Japanese.

quote.translation: There are, of course, many cases in which what was at first thought to be a contingency of sound is resolved into necessity .
